section_summary.extract_value: This brief discussion interprets findings from a single experiment showing that the guilt manipulation produced an indirect effect (via post-test guilt) on body anxiety but no significant direct effect; the effect appears specific to guilt rather than general negative affect. The authors note methodological limitations—guilt and body anxiety were measured at post-test (cross-sectional mediation), pre-test guilt was not measured, and only some participants experienced induced guilt—limiting causal inference and suggesting need for longitudinal and replication work.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'The total effect of the guilt condition on body anxiety was not significant and this is due to the fact that the direct effect is negligible and not significant.'; 'There was no main effect of the guilt manipulation on post-test body anxiety, and the mediation analysis presented utilizes post-test guilt as part of the indirect effect: the mediator (guilt) is measured at the same time (post-test) as the proposed outcome variable (body anxiety).'
